newsitem.title: USA: Most IMM currency futures end higher, off peaks.
newsitem.headline: Most IMM currency futures end higher, off peaks.

text.p: Most IMM currency futures ended slightly higher and just off daily peaks after moderate-volume daily trading.
Brokers tied the creep higher in most units partly to the gain-cutting in U.S. stocks, which slowly pulled back from their morning peaks and briefly visited afternoon lows.
Marks also garnered support from technicals and covering by day-shorts after proving unable to follow through decisively on the downside during the morning's pullback.
Afternoon comments by Bundesbank council member Helmut Hesse also gave marks a lift, brokers said.
Hesse said the Bundesbank has no choice but to insist on strict interpretation of the Maastricht criteria for joining European Economic and Monetary Union.

"That's as good an excuse as I've heard," said one slightly cynical floor broker of reasons other than technicals for the mark's drift upward. "If it's (EMU criteria) fudged, it boils down to a watered-down EMU and a watered-down mark."

The June mark early hit a new contract low at $0.5780 as the dollar rallied to 1.7350 spot. But futures stopped short of even touching Monday's peak and thus failed to form a classic key reversal that might have made some bears skittish.
Marks had slumped after Bundesbank chief economist Otmar Issing said the Euro launch could cause shifts from mark to dollar investments.
Rallies in U.S. debt and equity markets following tame March consumer price index (CPI) figures weighed down currencies early on.
CPI rose 0.1 percent overall and gained 0.2 percent in the core rate, slightly lower than forecasts for respective gains of 0.2 percent and 0.3 percent.
Uncertainty about EMU sent some players into sterling, brokers added.

The European Monetary Institute Tuesday in its annual report said the convergence of debt and deficit levels among many European Union countries remained far from satisfactory and that debt consolidation efforts were relying too much on revenue rather than spending cuts.

June yen ended up $0.000022 at $0.008003, marks rose $0.0010 to $0.5819, Swiss francs rose $0.0018 to $0.6872, pound rallied $0.0072 to $1.6272, Canadian dollar rose $0.0011 to $0.7186, Aussie dollar lost $0.0052 to $0.7739, Mexican peso rose $0.000350 to $0.122775.
